title: Kleiner (Fried Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, white sugar or powdered sugar, and cream.

ingredients.name: half a Pound white Sugar or dried and crushed Powdered Sugar
ingredients.sourceText: half a Pound white Sugar or dried and crushed Powdered Sugar

steps: Whip 6 Egg Yolks, 2 whole Eggs, and half a Pound white Sugar or dried and crushed Powdered Sugar well and stir with {{source-3}} and 1 Tablespoon clarified Butter
Add as much of {{source-5}} as you can incorporate; work the rest in on the board until the batter releases from the board and hands
Roll out very thin with Flour on the outside and cut into oblong pieces, best with a pastry wheel, so the cakes become notched at the edge
Cut a slit in the middle of each piece and push one end of the cake through it, so that it becomes twisted in the middle
Fry very light

title: Klejner (Danish Fried Pastry Strips)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, egg whites, and powdered sugar.
steps: Mix together egg yolks, egg whites, powdered sugar, butter, and lemon zest with a wooden spoon
When well mixed, stir in the flour until a smooth dough forms
Roll out the dough to the thickness of a five-øre coin
Cut strips 2 fingers wide and 4 inches long using a pastry wheel
Cut a slit in the center of each strip and pull one end through
Fry in melted butter or fat until golden brown
Turn during frying, remove and drain on paper so the butter runs off

title: Klidkager (Bran Cakes)
description: A cake made with rye, yeast, and caraway seeds.

ingredients.name: a few spoonfuls gluten flour (if available)
ingredients.sourceText: a few spoonfuls gluten flour (if available)

steps: The evening before the cakes are to be baked, work together {{source-0}}, a few spoonfuls gluten flour if available, {{source-2}}, 4 eggs, {{source-4}}, 5 quints pressed yeast, a handful salt, a handful caraway seeds, 5.5 measures boiled, cooled water and 0.5 measure vinegar into a dough.

Before baking, press the dough out on a pan with the hand to the thickness of a biscuit, roll thin and smooth with a bottle and cut into round or square small cakes before the pan is placed in the oven.
When the dough has dried a little on the pan, loosen all the cakes with a thin knife and later turn them so they can also dry on the side facing the pan.

title: Klipfisk-Budding (Dried Cod Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cod, egg yolks, and rusks.
steps: Soak the dried cod in water the evening before or at least in the morning.
Boil it and chop it fine; for each deep plate full of chopped fish use 8 egg yolks.
Soak 8 rusks in flour, let stand covered for some time, and then rub them together with the egg yolks and enough milk to make a consistency like ordinary pancake batter.
Add 0.5 pound of melted butter (reserve the salt), 1 cup of well-cleaned currants, then the fish, and lastly the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Immediately pour into the buttered form and boil for 2 hours.

title: Klipfiske-Budding (Salt Cod Pudding)
description: A pudding made with salt, margarine, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: finely chopped, cooked salt cod
ingredients.sourceText: 375 grams finely chopped, cooked salt cod

steps: 0.25 kilogram of flour is baked in 0.25 kilogram of margarine together with 375 grams of finely chopped, cooked salt cod and diluted with just under 0.75 liter of boiling milk.
When the batter is slightly cooled, it is stirred with 10 egg yolks, salt, ground white pepper, 125 grams of plucked and scalded raisins, and finally with the beaten egg whites.
The pudding is eaten with melted or creamed butter.
Salt cod pudding can also be made as bread pudding, with the fish stirred into it.

description: A sauce made with lamb, capers, and salt.

ingredients.name: A lamb shank with clear, white and hard fat
ingredients.sourceText: A lamb shank with clear, white and hard fat

steps: Put a handful of salt in a roomy pot with boiling water.
Choose a lamb shank with clear, white and hard fat, wash it and rub it thoroughly with salt.

Make a sauce from a pint of boiling milk, thickened with flour; add butter, salt, pepper and 2 spoonfuls of capers, and serve the meat with it.

title: Kogt Farseret Hvidkaal (Boiled Stuffed White Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, forcemeat, and melted butter or sauce or butter or flour or broth.

ingredients.name: melted butter or sauce made from butter, flour, and broth
ingredients.sourceText: melted butter or sauce made from butter, flour, and broth

steps: Remove the outer loose leaves from a good firm cabbage head
Cut a lid around the stem large enough to hollow out the head
Fill the forcemeat inside, leaving room for it to rise
Place the lid on and cover with a few of the removed leaves
Bind the head with twine and place in a pot with plenty of boiling salted water
Boil for 3 to 3.5 hours
When serving, remove the lid and place the head with forcemeat facing down on the platter
Serve with melted butter or sauce made from butter, flour, and the broth
The hollowed cabbage can be cooked with the head and arranged around it, or prepared together with cabbage broth into a brown cabbage soup with the addition of Maggi bouillon cubes

title: Kogt Fugl med Østers-Sauce (Boiled Fowl with Oyster Sauce)
description: A sauce made with fowl, oyster, and oysters.
steps: Clean the fowl but do not stuff.
Place in enough boiling water to cover the fowl.
Simmer carefully until the fowl is cooked.
When nearly done, prepare the oyster sauce: bring one quart of oysters to boil in their own liquid.
Strain the oysters; reserve the liquid and wash the oysters in cold water.
Mix one ounce of butter and one ounce of flour together over heat until they form a white paste, being careful not to brown.
Stir in enough of the oyster sauce and enough broth from the fowl to make the sauce the consistency of melted butter.
Season with salt, white pepper, and grated nutmeg.
Add the oysters and pour over the fowl.
Sprinkle finely chopped parsley over all.
This dish can also be made with hens and chickens.

description: Prepared with pike, vinegar, and potatoes.

title: Kogt Hummer (Boiled Lobster)
description: Prepared with lobster, water, and salt.
steps: Set a pot over the fire with plenty of water and salt.
When the water is boiling, add the live lobsters with their claws tied together, after rinsing them in cold water.
Boil over strong heat until the legs can be removed. Do not cook longer or the meat will become stringy.
Skim the water during cooking.
Remove the pot from the fire and let the lobsters cool until half-cold.
Remove the lobsters and crack the back and tail lengthwise and the claws crosswise.
Serve cold with chopped parsley, pepper, vinegar and fine oil, along with fine green salad leaves.

title: Kogt Hummer (Boiled Lobster)
description: Prepared with lobster and water.
steps: Place the lobster in cold water and bring to a boil.
The lobster suffers less this way as it dies as soon as the water becomes warm, and its meat will be more tender.
Cook for 15 to 30 minutes depending on its size; very large ones may need an hour.
When cooked, remove it and split lengthwise from head to tail.
Remove the stomach (which follows right after the head) and the dark or bluish vein that runs from near the head to the end of the tail.

title: Kogt Laks (Boiled Salmon)
description: Prepared with salmon, peppercorns, and bay leaves.
steps: Before cleaning, place the salmon in cold water. Scrape it with a knife from the head toward the tail without loosening the scales.
Make a small crosswise cut at the vent fin nearest the tail, and remove the entrails from the opening near the head without opening the belly.
Rinse the fish thoroughly in several changes of cold water and clean the inside well.
Sprinkle with salt and let stand for a couple of hours before cooking.

The salmon is best when cooked whole, but may also be cut into round slices about an inch thick, which are reassembled into the original form when served. Alternatively, the fish may be split while raw by following the backbone from the tail through the head with a sharp knife for a beautiful presentation on two platters.
For cooking time, allow 5 to 6 minutes per inch of thickness.

If cooking whole without a fish kettle, use a fish rack or lay a coarse cloth in the bottom of the pot large enough to hang over the sides. Place a plate on the cloth and lay the fish on it for easy removal when plated.
For whole fish, place in enough cold water to just cover. For cut fish, place in boiling water with vinegar (2½ dl or 1 pint per 5 to 6 liters of water), whole peppercorns, bay leaves, and salt.
Keep the cooking at an even temperature, skim well during cooking, and let the fish rest in the water for a few minutes before serving.

Serve on a warm platter lined with a fish rack and a folded napkin. Garnish the head and tail with parsley and lemon slices or boiled crayfish. The platter may be further garnished with croutons filled with a ragout of shrimp, crayfish, lobster, or oysters, or the ragout may be served in gratinée shells arranged around the edge of the platter.

title: Kogt Lammebryst (Boiled Lamb Breast)
description: Prepared with lamb, broth, and salt.
steps: From a lamb forequarter, remove the brisket, cut off the chops, and break and remove the breastbones along with the brisket in smaller pieces.
Wash the pieces well and place them over heat in cold water with salt and a broth bundle.
Skim well and cook tender in the course of about an hour.
Boiled lamb meat, especially the leg, is excellent served with cream horseradish sauce (see Nr. 798).

title: Kogt Torsk (Boiled Cod)
description: Prepared with cod, vinegar, and salt.
steps: Large cod should be cooked whole and placed in cold water with salt and a little vinegar to make the flesh firmer, while smaller cod are cut in half and placed in boiling water.

When the cod is slaughtered, make a cut at the nape and one at the tail, then hold it under running water, letting the water stream rinse it well, which causes the muscles to contract and the fish to become firmer.
Open the belly, remove the innards, and cook the liver, roe, or milt together with the fish. Remove the gall bladder carefully.
Scrape the fish from the tail upward, clean it well inside, and after sufficient rinsing, make 2 or 3 cuts on each side of the skin so it does not burst during cooking.
Let it stand with salt for a couple of hours before cooking, which must take place without a lid, otherwise the fish becomes loose and falls apart.
When plating, place a fish rack on the platter and over it a folded napkin, upon which the cod is laid.
Garnish at the head and tail with liver, roe, or sliced milt, between which parsley is inserted.
Place boiled potatoes on the sides of the cod.

title: Kogt, Farseret Kalvebryst (Boiled Stuffed Veal Breast)
description: Prepared with veal, forcemeat or veal or pork, and salt.
steps: Remove the bones with a sharp knife.
Spread a layer of forcemeat (which should not be beaten too fine) over the meat.
Roll the breast tightly together and sew it closed to prevent the forcemeat from escaping during cooking.
Place in boiling salted water and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours.
Remove the thread and slice the meat, garnishing with parsley.
Use the cooking liquid partly for sauce and partly for a light soup that does not require much strength.

title: Kogte Høns med Ris, Karri eller Champignons (Boiled Hens with Rice, Curry, or Mushrooms)
description: Prepared with rice, hen, and celery.
steps: Cut the hen into pieces and wash in lukewarm water.
Boil until tender in water and salt.
Make a sauce from the strained cooking broth with celery root and parsley roots.
Thicken the sauce with flour and butter.
Clean half a pound of rice and cook slowly over steady heat with constant stirring.
Place the chicken in the sauce and arrange with a ring of cooked rice around the edge of the platter.
If desired, add a little curry to the sauce.
Alternatively, arrange the boiled hen in a mushroom sauce (see recipe 240).

title: Kogte Karper (Boiled Carp)
description: Prepared with carp, peppercorns, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: Vinegar (3¾ dl or 1½ pint per 2 to 3 carp)
ingredients.sourceText: Vinegar (3¾ dl or 1½ pint per 2 to 3 carp)

steps: Clean the carp, scraping the scales lightly and leaving them on. The fish may be cooked whole or split, with bones remaining on one half.
After thorough rinsing, sprinkle the carp with salt and let stand for one hour.
Place in a casserole and pour over boiling vinegar (3¾ dl or 1½ pint per 2 to 3 carp). Turn the fish regularly and let stand for a good quarter hour.
Add whole peppercorns, a couple of bay leaves, a bunch of parsley, and enough water to cook the fish.
Bring to a rapid boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 3 quarters of an hour to 1 hour, depending on the size of the fish.
Serve with cold cream and horseradish sauce, melted butter, and boiled potatoes. Garnish with boiled crayfish, lemon slices, and parsley.

title: Kogte Ris (Cooked Rice)
description: Prepared with rice, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: Rice (1 1/4 L or about 1 pint per 10 persons)
ingredients.sourceText: Rice (1 1/4 L or about 1 pint per 10 persons)

steps: Rinse the rice first in cold and then in warm water
Place it in abundant boiling salted water
When it is so tender that it can easily be pressed apart, drain the water from it
Fill the pot with cold water and stir the rice until it is completely separated
Drain the water and cover with a lid
Keep at heat until serving
Alternatively, after cooking, spread the rice on a colander and cover with cold water, then place in a warm oven, stirring regularly with a fork until it is separated and all water has evaporated

title: Kogte Selleriſtiſke (Boiled Celery Stalks)
description: Prepared with celery, carrot, and bouillon.
steps: Remove the green leaves from the stalks, cut the stalks to a length of 4 inches
Boil for 10 minutes in water, place in cold water, clean well, rinse in several changes of water, and set to drain
Tie the stalks together in groups of two or three, cook with ½ Pint bouillon, ½ Pint water, carrot, spices, and a little butter
Cook very gently for 2 hours covered
Drain and arrange
Make a roux with butter and flour, thin with the remaining bouillon, which is reduced to 3 spoonfuls, strain, and pour over the stalks
Serve as a vegetable or as an independent course

title: Kold Appelsin-Budding (Cold Orange Pudding)
description: A pudding made with powdered sugar, rind, and juice.

ingredients.name: juice of 6 oranges and 2 large lemons
ingredients.sourceText: juice of 6 oranges and 2 large lemons

steps: To {{source-0}} add the grated rind of 2 oranges and 2 lemons, also the juice of 6 oranges and 2 large lemons, 1 bottle white wine, 12 kvint isinglass and 6 egg yolks.
Stir everything well together and place over the fire, bringing to a boil while stirring constantly.
Pour the mixture into a mold and let stand for a few hours in a cold place.
The pudding is served with vanilla cream.
When the pudding is taken from the fire, one can also carefully fold in 2 pægle sweet cream that has been whipped to stiff peaks.

title: Kold Lever-Postej (Cold Liver Pâté)
description: Prepared with veal liver, pork fat, and broth.

ingredients.sourceText: Pork fat from the loin, finely chopped, 3/4 pound per pound of liver

steps: Wash and cook the veal liver
Cool it thoroughly
Grate it finely
For each pound of grated liver, take 3/4 pound of finely chopped pork fat from the loin
Work everything together well with pepper and salt
Thin with some of the broth in which the liver was cooked and with sweet cream until it becomes smooth and spongy
Place in a buttered mold
Bake for 1 hour in a warm oven
Cool thoroughly
When the pâté is to be served, dip the mold in boiling water to loosen it
Serve as an accompaniment to open-faced sandwiches
Optional: add finely chopped onion to the liver mixture, or line the mold with very thin bacon slices
Note: Pork liver or game liver can be used instead of veal liver

title: Kold Postej af Vildt (Cold Game Pâté)
description: Prepared with game, bacon, and meat.

ingredients.name: Breast meat from game bird, finely chopped
ingredients.sourceText: Breast meat from game bird, finely chopped

ingredients.name: Pork fatback, finely chopped, equal amount to breast meat
ingredients.sourceText: Pork fatback, finely chopped, equal amount to breast meat

steps: Grease a casserole with butter and line with butter dough
Line the bottom and sides with thin bacon slices
Pluck and clean the game bird thoroughly
Scrape all meat from the breast and chop very finely with an equal amount of pork fatback, 2 onions, pepper, 4 whole eggs, {{source-9}}, a little crushed thyme, and {{source-11}}
Mix everything together well
Layer the forcemeat mixture in the bottom, then a layer of game, then forcemeat again, then a layer of pitted olives, and continue alternating until the mold is nearly full
Top with a layer of butter dough, pressed firmly at the sides
Place in a warm oven and bake for 30 minutes
Remove and cut an opening in the center
Fill this opening with good, strong hot bouillon
Return to the oven and bake for another 2 hours, occasionally pouring hot bouillon into the opening
Remove from oven and let cool until half-cold
Place a light press on top and leave until the next day
Place the casserole in hot water to loosen the pâté and turn it out onto a serving dish
Serve with robust vegetables

Serve very hot, garnished with puff pastry strips, cooked apple halves, or glazed chestnuts.

Pour in as much boiling water as needed for the sauce.
Cook the giblets until tender under a lid for at least 2 hours.
Remove the carrots and skim the fat from the gravy.
Finish the sauce with sherry and thicken further with potato starch mixed in water.
Serve very hot, garnished with puff pastry strips, cooked apple halves, or glazed chestnuts.

title: Kraase-Suppe (Goose Giblet Soup)
description: A soup made with goose, apples, and prunes.

ingredients.name: (20 skein) butter or vegetable margarine
ingredients.sourceText: 100 g (20 skein) butter or vegetable margarine

steps: After the giblets are cleaned, split the heads, cut off the beaks, and remove the brains and eyes.
Chop the wings into 2 pieces and the neck with skin into 3 pieces.
Remove the windpipe and gullet, and clean the heart of blood.
Split the giblets, clean, and scald together with the feet (claws removed) and remove the outer skin, as well as the thick membrane on the inside of the giblets.
When sufficiently cleaned and washed, place in cold water with salt so it reaches the level of the giblets.
When boiling, skim the soup, then add whisks and vegetables as mentioned for goose soup.
As soon as the giblets are tender, which takes 2-3 hours, strain most of the soup away, leaving just a little in the pot to keep the giblets warm.
Bake {{source-4}} in {{source-3}} and thin with the strained soup and the water in which the apples and prunes were cooked.
Season with vinegar and sugar to taste and can be mixed with Maggi bouillon cubes.
Pour the boiling soup into the tureen over rolls, apples, prunes, and the cut vegetables.
The giblets can be served either in the soup or separately; garnish the platter with parsley.

title: Kraasesuppe og Andesuppe (Goose and Duck Offal Soup)
description: A soup made with geese or ducks, vegetables, and apple.
steps: Clean the offal thoroughly, removing the thick inner membrane and cutting into 2 or 4 pieces
Clean the heads by splitting and removing the tongues, neck, and outermost wing joints, carefully plucking out fine feathers
Scald the feet and remove the outer skin
Clean the liver and heart
Place all cleaned and rinsed offal in a pot with 5 pots cold water and a little salt
Bring to boil and skim
Add soup vegetables and roots
Simmer until the offal is tender
Remove the offal and keep warm for serving with the soup
Remove the roots, cut into pieces, and place in the tureen
Strain the soup and return to heat for a boil with peeled apple pieces, some washed prunes, and a small piece of ginger
When the apples are tender, remove from heat and season with sugar, vinegar, and salt to taste
For duck soup, old ducks may also be used; one duck is usually sufficient for 6 portions

title: Kraaſepostei (Goose Giblet Pâté)
description: Prepared with goose, pastry, and carrots.
steps: Simmer the giblets for 5 minutes in water with a little salt, rinse, drain on a sieve, place in a casserole with the vegetables and seasonings, moisten with sufficient bouillon or water and a little soy sauce and stew very gently over a weak heat 1.5 hours or longer or shorter according to the age of the geese.

When the giblets are cooked, drain them; cut them together with the vegetables into pieces of a couple of inches length. The liver is cooked less. Arrange in a pâté mold that has been lined with farce.
Reduce the bouillon in which the giblets were cooked to a suitably thick sauce, from which the fat is skimmed well. Pour the sauce into the mold, cover the mold with pastry dough and bake. Serve.

title: Krebse-Suppe (Crayfish Soup)
description: A soup made with crayfish, meat, and rice flour.
steps: Boil the crayfish as usual.

Pick out the meat from the tails, heads and claws; crush the shells and all the small bones finely with a little butter, place on the fire and blanch well, but not too long, so as to avoid a bad taste, and moisten slightly with meat broth, which does not need to be strong, until it stands over this.
When it has cooked a little, strain it, place it back on the fire with the same amount of broth, and after a good boiling strain it again into the dark portion.

Let the soup stand awhile so that you can skim off the red butter; in this stir in approximately two ounces of rice flour, which is added to the crayfish soup when this, mixed with the remaining meat broth, boils again.
Use only white root vegetables or asparagus.
It is eaten either with bread dumplings, into which the chopped crayfish claws and heads are stirred, or with fish dumplings.
The shells of the crayfish heads are filled with some of the dumpling dough and cooked in the soup.
After the dark vein is removed from the tails, these whole tails are placed on the finished soup, but must not be cooked with it.

title: Krebsesuppe eller Hummersuppe (Crayfish or Lobster Soup)
description: A soup made with crayfish, wheat flour, and crayfish or lobster or bouillon.
steps: Wash the crayfish and place in boiling salted water. Cook for approximately a quarter hour until done.
Remove and let cool, then shell them. Set aside the tails (removing the intestine) and some of the largest claws. Clean the 20 to 24 finest heads well and place in cold water.
Finely pound all remaining debris and shells with 1/4 pound of butter.
Place in a saucepan and sauté with constant stirring so it does not burn.
Dilute with the crayfish bouillon so it stands well above the shells and cook until the red butter floats on top. Skim this during cooking as it appears.

Place the crayfish butter in a saucepan with 1 tablespoon of wheat flour and cook together, then dilute with the strained crayfish bouillon and good bouillon until it makes between 4 and 5 pots total.
Fill the cleaned empty head shells with fish forcemeat, boil in salted water, clean them and add to the soup along with the tails and large claws. Small fish balls may also be added.
In the tureen, beat 4 egg yolks with 6 tablespoons of good sweet cream, then carefully add the soup a little at a time under continuous beating.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

For lobster soup, prepare in the same manner but also add 1 pound of asparagus cut into pieces about one inch long, along with a little of the asparagus water, which is brought to a boil with the soup.

title: Kringler til The og Kaffe (Kringler for Tea and Coffee)
description: Prepared with yeast, wheat flour, and melted butter.
steps: Warm 1 pint milk and set with 2 cents yeast dissolved in a little of the milk plus as much fine wheat flour to make dough of the usual thickness and evenness.

Set in a warm place, and when well risen (which takes 2 to 3 hours), stir in {{source-3}}, {{source-4}}, a generous amount of chopped candied orange peel, lemon zest, and a handful of sugar and 3 eggs.
Stir in flour until the dough is stiff enough to knead but not more.
When kneaded so it no longer sticks to the fingers, divide into three parts, roll out long and thin, and braid the dough in an ordinary braid that is long enough to fit around inside a bread pan.
Set to rise again, and when risen, brush with egg.

title: Krustader (Crusted Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with clarified butter, beer, and flour.
steps: Mix flour, clarified butter, egg, white beer, and water to form a smooth batter of the consistency of pancake batter
Heat the croustade iron well in boiling butter or clarified fat
Dip the iron in the batter
Place it back in the hot butter or fat and fry until the croustade becomes a beautiful light brown
Remove from the iron carefully with a thin knife at the edge of the iron
Place upside down on a plate until needed (preferably the same day)
If croustades must be kept, cover them so they do not lose their crispness
Fill with similar filling as used for small pâtés
Allow 8 to 10 per serving

title: Krustader (Fried Pastry Shells)
description: A pastry dish made with egg white, powdered sugar, and clarified butter.

ingredients.name: Clarified butter or Palmin for frying
ingredients.sourceText: Clarified butter or Palmin for frying

steps: Mix flour, cold water, egg white, powdered sugar, and eggs into a thin pancake batter
Heat clarified butter or Palmin in a pot with a krustader iron
Do not heat the Palmin so strongly that it steams
Pour batter into as many small cups as there are forms on the iron
Dip the iron into the batter, not quite to the rim
Keep in the hot fat and fry until the shells are light brown
Loosen with a fork or larding needle and place upside down on paper to drain the fat
Pour the remaining fat through a sieve
The shells can be stored in metal boxes for a long time, but must be placed in a warm oven before filling is added

title: Kræmmerhuse (Cream-Filled Cone Cakes)
description: A cake made with egg whites, margarine, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: Preserved strawberries, cherries, raspberry jam, currant or gooseberry jelly
ingredients.sourceText: Preserved strawberries, cherries, raspberry jam, currant or gooseberry jelly

steps: Melt the margarine; while hot, stir in the powdered sugar and flour, and finally 8 beaten egg whites.
The baking sheet must be warm; brush it well and place the dough on it with a teaspoon, with large intervals.
Spread the dough with a spoon into elongated cakes and bake quickly in a well-heated oven; they should have a beautiful golden-brown color.

When the cakes are finished but still in the oven, loosen them with a knife and twist into the form of a cone, which must be done very quickly, as the cakes otherwise break and cannot be bent once cooled.

Store in a tin box and fill with whipped cream just before serving, as they otherwise become soft. Preserved strawberries, cherry jam, raspberry jam, or currant or gooseberry jelly may be served alongside.

title: Kv eder (Quinces)
description: Prepared with quinces, sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: sugar, white or brown
ingredients.sourceText: One pound sugar, white or brown

steps: Place the quinces in boiling water and cook until they begin to soften.
Remove, peel, and cut according to size into 4 or 8 pieces.
Remove the seed cavities and all the hard matter surrounding them; weigh the pieces.
For 1 pound quinces, take 1 pound sugar, white or brown, and place on heat with one pint water.
When the first scum is removed, add the quinces and skim well.
Cook evenly for one hour or longer, if needed, until they are completely tender and the syrup is even.
Pour into a vessel, spread cloth over, and after a day, cover with paper dipped in brandy and tie.

title: Kv eder Nr. 2 (Quinces No. 2)
description: Prepared with quinces, brown sugar, and water.

ingredients.name: white or brown sugar
ingredients.sourceText: One pound white or brown sugar

steps: Dry the quinces, remove the peelings, and weigh them.
For 1 pound peelings, take 1 pint water; cook very evenly for one hour, then strain.
Cut the quinces into 4 to 8 pieces, remove the seed cavities and all hard matter, and weigh.
For 1 pound quinces, take 1 pound white or brown sugar and place in the water that was strained from the peelings.
When melted, add the quinces and cook covered over a good, even heat, not flame, stirring regularly until tender.
This may take a couple of hours.
By this even cooking under closed lid, the quinces will turn red; if not, a little cherry juice may be added.
Pour into a vessel and tie as usual.

title: Kvædesaft (Quince Syrup)
description: Prepared with quinces and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: 575 gr (1/4 lb) powdered sugar per 1 liter (1 pot) juice
ingredients.sourceText: 575 gr (1/4 lb) powdered sugar per 1 liter (1 pot) juice

steps: Dry the quinces and cut into very small pieces, cutting away the core.
Put them in a pot and pour on enough water so it is level with the fruit.
Boil the quinces until completely soft, then strain through a jelly cloth and let hang for several hours.
Measure the drained juice and boil with the sugar for a quarter hour.
Skim well during boiling; pour hot into dry bottles, which are tied with parchment paper as soon as they are filled.
The quince pulp left in the cloth is boiled in water and used for soup or similar dishes.
Quince syrup can be made into an excellent dessert by adding isinglass and filling into molds.

ingredients.sourceText: whipped cream and strawberry or raspberry jam (optional)

steps: Mix the flour with some of the buttermilk in the bottom of the pot
Add the remaining cold buttermilk with citrus peel, cinnamon, and scalded raisins or currants

Beat 3 egg yolks with sugar in a tureen
Pour the soup into the egg mixture
Serve immediately
Optional: add finely crushed almonds
Optional: serve separately with whipped cream and strawberry or raspberry jam, omitting the raisins and currants

title: Kærnemælk-Suppe med Maizena (Buttermilk Soup with Cornstarch)
description: A soup made with buttermilk, cornstarch, and powdered sugar.
steps: For each liter of buttermilk, use one good tablespoon of cornstarch
Mix the cornstarch in some of the cold milk
Pour under stirring into the remaining boiling milk
Bring to a boil
Stir in a tureen where 1 egg yolk per liter of milk has been mixed with powdered sugar
Add a little vanilla essence
Optional: the soup can be served cold as a dessert after a meat course, with whipped cream folded in, and strawberry or raspberry jam and small macaroons served alongside

description: Prepared with buttermilk, egg yolks, and powdered sugar.

title: Kød-Boller i brun Sauce, garneret med overskaarne Æg (Meatballs in Brown Sauce, Garnished with Sliced Eggs)
description: A sauce made with trimmings, onion, and stock.

ingredients.name: Sinews and trimmings from meat used for forcemeat
ingredients.sourceText: Sinews and trimmings from meat used for forcemeat

steps: Boil the sinews and other trimmings from the meat in salted water
When strained and brought to a boil again, form oval-shaped balls with a spoon
To make good balls, ensure they do not boil longer than necessary, which depends on the size of the balls, as the forcemeat otherwise easily loses its juiciness and becomes hard and dry
Make the sauce from browned butter, add a large grated onion, paprika and flour; thin with the stock and add wine, food coloring and a little tomato purée
Pour the sauce over the balls
Since the sauce for the balls should be strong and piquant, use Maggi bouillon cubes to improve it

title: Kød-Boller i Selleri-Sauce (Meatballs in Celery Sauce)
description: A sauce made with celery, water or stock, and forcemeat.
steps: Peel the celery, rinse well and cut into small cubes
Boil the celery cubes in water or stock
When the celery is cooked, remove it
Boil the meatballs in the stock
For the sauce, brown butter and flour, thin with the strained stock and bind at the end with a couple of egg yolks; add ground white pepper and a glass of sherry
Serve with puff pastry strips

title: Kød-Jærpe (Meat Jerpe)
description: Prepared with pork, bacon, and potatoes.

ingredients.name: soup made from bones and trimmings
ingredients.sourceText: soup made from bones and trimmings

steps: Mince the meat very finely together with the bacon.
Season with ginger, pepper, and salt.
Knead the mixture by hand or with a spoon.
Add 6-8 grated boiled potatoes and 2-3 eggs.
Add enough cream or good milk to achieve a proper consistency for forming into a fillet shape.
Place in a roasting pan, give it an oblong shape, and roast in a hot oven for one hour.
Baste frequently with soup made from bones and trimmings.
Make sauce from browned butter and flour thinned with gravy.
Slice the roast and garnish with warm potato salad.

title: Kødbudding med Makkaroni og Skinke (Meat Pudding with Macaroni and Ham)
description: A pudding made with macaroni, meat, and bouillon.
steps: Cook {{source-0}} in just enough thin bouillon to barely cover it until tender, but not overcooked.
Cook smoked ham well and it should not be too salty.
When cold, thickly line a pudding mold with meat farce.
Layer small slices of the lean part of the ham and the macaroni with their sauce, then meat farce over.
You can either stir a little rinsed butter into the macaroni while hot, or leave a little of the fat on the ham pieces as desired.
It must cook for at least 3 hours.

title: Lagkage (Layer Cake)
description: A cake made with powdered sugar, egg yolks, and lemon.
steps: Stir {{source-0}} to a salve and add {{source-1}}, stirring for a good half hour until white
Stir for half an hour with 8 egg yolks until quite light
Add 1/2 pound fine Hungarian flour and the grated yellow zest and strained juice of 1 large lemon
Finally add the egg whites after whipping to stiff peaks
Roll out this batter and bake into 8 sheets, either in 8 special forms or in 8 paper forms; in both cases butter the forms and the oven should be very hot
When the layers are baked a fine pale brown, remove from the oven and set to cool
The given amount is for 2 cakes, as each uses 4 layers, between which white wine cream is placed (vanilla cream easily becomes sour)
Decorate on top with sugar glaze

description: Prepared with lamb, asparagus, and shrimp.
steps: Cut the meat into appropriately small pieces, rinse in cold water and blanch.
Place over heat in cold water with salt, skim and cook with a good soup whisk; when tender, some of the broth is drained off, the rest remains with the meat so it can be kept warm.

Brown butter and flour and thin with broth mixed with asparagus water into a smooth sauce, which is thickened with 3-4 egg yolks.
At serving, arrange the asparagus and the cooked, peeled shrimp between the meat, and pour the sauce over.

steps: While lambs are small, it does not matter if you choose meat from a young ewe or wether lamb; but later the latter often acquire a less pleasant woolly taste, so the former are to be preferred.
For roasting, choose the loin with attached back.
Remove the shank, break the bones and back, then beat the roast lightly with a meat mallet, rub with salt and lard with fine parsley.
Place it in a warm oven in a pan with salt, butter and a little water.
Lay a piece of white writing paper, dipped in butter or water, over the roast.
When the roast has cooked somewhat and the heat is less strong, remove the paper and baste it with the sauce.
Roasting takes 1 to 2 hours depending on the size of the roast, and you must be careful that it does not burn.
Skim the fat from the sauce, thicken it with a little flour, strain and serve to the roast together with potatoes and salad.

title: Lammebryst i Grønnærter (Lamb Breast with Green Peas)
description: Prepared with lamb, peas, and carrots.

ingredients.name: 2½ to 3 Kg (5 to 6 S) lamb meat
ingredients.sourceText: 2½ to 3 Kg (5 to 6 S) lamb meat

steps: Cut the meat into smaller pieces as for fricassée.
After washing them, scald them in boiling water and place them in a pot.
Pour 1 L (1 Pot) boiling water over the meat with a little salt, and only when the broth is completely skimmed, add the peas.
Cook the meat with the peas tender under a lid and over gentle heat, but it must be constantly watched so the water does not evaporate and the meat and peas burn on.
If the liquid shrinks away, pour a little more broth or water into the pot.
The meat must be stirred to become tender, so that the top pieces come to the bottom of the pot.
When it is nearly done, add 125 Gr (¼ S) butter along with salt and sugar, if the peas are not sufficiently sweet in themselves.
Serve meat and peas together on a platter, and the dish can be garnished with small boiled carrots.

title: Lammesteg (Roast Lamb)
description: Prepared with lamb, cream, and butter.

ingredients.name: lamb hindquarter with kidney piece
ingredients.sourceText: 3.5 kg lamb hindquarter with kidney piece

steps: The hindquarter with kidney piece is generally what is used for roast lamb, and to have the proper form, it should be cut so that 3 of the ribs follow with the roast.
These ribs are given a break on the inside with an axe, so the roast can lie well on the dish.
The shank is cut off, and the back is broken on the underside at appropriate intervals to ease carving, but not so deeply that the back comes apart.
With a pointed knife, holes are pierced along the back and leg, into which parsley is inserted together with a little butter; some of the parsley must be visible over the meat.
On the roasting pan, which is placed in the hot oven, a little meat gravy or butter is laid before the roast is placed on it.
The roast is sprinkled with salt and must stand thus for about 10 minutes; then boiling water is poured on the pan, and the roast is basted well.
Usually one counts 1.5 hours of roasting for a lamb roast of 2.5 kg.
For the sauce, butter is browned, which is baked with flour, thinned with the strained drippings with the fat skimmed off.
The sauce must not be too dark, and after it has boiled well, a little raw cream and a slice of cold butter can be added, but this is not necessary.
Roast lamb can be served garnished with a bouquet of parsley, salad or flowers, pierced with a skewer, which is fastened in the shank joint at the tail part.

title: Leverpostej (Liver Pâté) (Made as Strasbourg-style Goose Liver Pâté)
description: Prepared with liver, pork fat, and margarine.
steps: Mince the pork fat very finely.
Make a roux by cooking the margarine and flour together, then thin it with milk to create a thick batter or soft gruel.
Add the minced pork fat to the batter.
Place the pot over very low heat to prevent burning and let the mixture cook very gently until the pork fat is rendered.
While the mixture cooks, prepare the liver.
Select the lightest livers, which are also the fattest, with a fragile membrane that breaks easily with finger pressure.
Wash the liver thoroughly and remove the membrane.
Scrape the liver so that no veins or connective tissue are included.
Mince the liver finely and place on a coarse, inverted sieve.
Gradually press the warm mixture through the sieve with the liver.
In the strained liver mixture, stir in 2 egg yolks, {{source-6}}, {{source-7}}, salt to taste, 1 grated small onion, and the whipped egg whites.
Fill molds (not completely full) and place on a baking sheet in a moderately warm oven.
Avoid high heat as it will form a hard crust on top.
Cover the molds with paper during baking.
Bake in a water bath for 1 hour.
If a layer of liquid fat forms on top of the hot pâté, do not pour it off as it will be reabsorbed.
Let rest until the next day.
Place the mold over a steaming kettle or pass it several times over a weak gas flame to loosen it from the sides.
Turn the pâté out of the mold.
In a gelatin mold, pour good, clear aspic mixed with isinglass.
When set, turn it over onto the liver pâté.
Decorate with parsley, pickled shallots, small onions, pickles, slices of cucumber, or other garnishes.

title: Leverpölse (Liver Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork liver, heart, and bread.

ingredients.name: meat without sinews and skin
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 pound meat without sinews and skin

ingredients.name: Nutmeg and white pepper in equal quantities, ground and mixed together
ingredients.sourceText: Nutmeg and white pepper in equal quantities, ground and mixed together

steps: After all sinews and membranes are removed, cut the liver and offal into square pieces of one inch size.
Melt the offal in a frying pan over gentle heat; mix salt and seasonings with the liver; stir everything together for 3 minutes over the heat and then set aside to cool.
Place the meat first 30 minutes in boiling water, then in cold water and cut into small cubes.
Pound the liver and offal, press through a steel sieve, then pound in a mortar into a fine mass together with the panade.
Add the cream and eggs little by little.
Season carefully with salt and spices; finally mix the meat cubes into the whole.

Fill the finished farce either into sausage casings and treat in the usual manner, after which it is eaten cold; or it can also be placed in a large, round or oblong mold that has been previously buttered and cooked evenly for 2 hours, after which the farce is set aside to cool and the mold is turned. Cut into slices and eaten cold.

title: Leverpølse (Liver Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork liver, pork fat, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: Sweet cream or cold bacon soup
ingredients.sourceText: Sweet cream or cold bacon soup

steps: Place a good pork liver in water and let it stand for one day so that the blood is completely drawn out.
Cook it then in some water with salt until it is tender, then take it up, set it aside to become cold, and remove the skin.
Then grate the liver finely, making sure that there are no small hard pieces in between.
From pork fat remove all sinews and skins, then scrape the fat so it becomes like butter.
Mix equal weight of this and of the grated liver well together with finely ground salt and white pepper.
Some shallot onions are cooked down in a little fat, and this is strained into the mass.
Stir with sweet cream or in the absence thereof with cold bacon soup until it has reached an appropriate thickness, then stuff firmly into cleaned intestines.
Tie these and sprinkle with salt, after which they stand 1 day.
They then get a brief cooking of a few minutes in warm water, are taken up and stirred.
Eaten cold with open-faced sandwiches.

title: Lincoln Budding (Lincoln Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cornstarch, margarine, and egg yolks.
steps: 250 grams of cornstarch is stirred into 0.25 liter of cold milk.
Just over 0.5 liter of milk is brought to a boil, the mixture is quickly stirred in, and cooked for a couple of minutes.

The pot is lifted from the heat, while 75 grams of cold margarine is stirred into the mass; this is poured into a dish in which 8 egg yolks have been stirred with 125 grams of powdered sugar, 1 teaspoonful of salt, 50 grams of finely cut orange peel, and grated zest of 0.5 lemon.
The beaten egg whites are stirred in last, and the batter is immediately poured into a mold buttered and sprinkled with breadcrumbs.
Bake 0.25 hour in the oven and serve in the mold.
Serve with fruit sauce or fruit compote.

title: Linser (Cream-Filled Tartlets)
description: A pastry dish made with cream, margarine, and powdered sugar.
steps: Knead together the flour, margarine, powdered sugar, and 4 egg yolks until a dough forms; let it rest for half an hour.
Roll out thinly and line small buttered baking forms.
Place 1 teaspoon cream in each form; arrange these closely together on the kitchen counter and cover with a large sheet of dough, thinly rolled out.
Trim the edges of the forms and place in the oven.
Bake for approximately half an hour. They can be prepared early in the day and baked later.
For the filling cream: beat 3 egg yolks with 3 tablespoons powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon flour, and vanilla essence. When {{source-8}} is added, continue as directed.
This portion yields 40 cakes.

Serve with raspberry juice or mixed fruit juice.

title: Makaroni-Salat (Macaroni Salad)
description: A salad made with macaroni, cream, and vinegar.
steps: Cook {{source-0}} tender in water with salt
Mix a lump of butter and 0.5 pint cream with vinegar, sugar and grated horseradish to taste
Add the macaroni (drained on a colander) to this sauce
Serve this salad cold

Add the macaroni (drained on a colander) and steam for 20 minutes, then serve immediately

title: Makaroni-Suppe à l'Italienne (Macaroni Soup Italian Style)
description: A soup made with macaroni, stock, and egg yolks.
steps: Cook the thin macaroni until tender in half of the soup for approximately 1/2 hour
Drain the macaroni and once cooled, cut it into very small pieces
Mix the soup in which the macaroni was cooked with the remaining soup and return the macaroni to it
As soon as it boils, lift the pot from the heat
Beat 6 egg yolks with {{source-3}}, 75 gr grated Parmesan cheese and a little ground white pepper
Add this mixture to the soup while stirring vigorously
Set the pot back over the heat for a couple of minutes while continuing to stir, but do not let it boil
Season with Madeira or Graves wine if desired
Serve immediately

title: Mandelbudding (Almond Pudding)
description: A pudding made with sweet almonds, bitter almonds, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: ¾ pægle finely ground wheat bread
ingredients.sourceText: ¾ pægle finely ground wheat bread

steps: Scald the sweet and bitter almonds, remove the skins and pound them fine in a mortar.
When nearly fine, add 36 kvint powdered sugar and a couple of tablespoons water, and pound again until the whole becomes like a stiff dough.
Take it out and stir in 1 pægle melted butter, ¾ pægle finely ground wheat bread and 8 beaten eggs.
Beat 5 egg whites to stiff peaks and fold into the mixture.
Butter a mold and sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
Pour the mixture in and place the mold in boiling water.
Cook the pudding for 2 hours.
Turn out onto a platter and serve with powdered sugar.

title: Mandelgrød (Almond Porridge)
description: Prepared with almonds, rice flour, and milk.

ingredients.name: Half a pound almonds, of which approximately 6 ounces are bitter
ingredients.sourceText: Half a pound almonds, of which approximately 6 ounces are bitter

steps: Scald and chop the almonds with a little lemon peel.
Place 3 pots of the sweet milk in an enameled pot smeared with cold butter at the bottom and cook over gentle heat.
Mix 1 pound of rice flour with the remaining 2 pots of cold milk.
When the milk in the pot begins to boil, add the mixed flour and almonds.
Stir the porridge continuously until fully cooked.
Stir in one-quarter pound of white vanilla sugar.
Pour into a large bowl to cool.
Serve cold with mixed fruit juice or diluted wine with sugar.

title: Marcipan (Marzipan)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, bitter almonds, and rose water or rum.
steps: Blanch the sweet and bitter almonds, remove the skin, rinse and dry in a cloth.
Pass this mass twice through an enameled meat grinder and then 2 more times with the flour sugar.
Now knead the almond paste with the flour sugar and rose water or rum.
Can be stored in parchment in a cool place.
Form figures from this fresh marzipan and decorate with a brush using confectioner's colors, which can be bought in small portions at the grocer's.
Place the finished marzipan on dishes and set in a cool place for a couple of days.
The marzipan should not be baked.

Strain the stock and thicken browned butter and flour with it to make the sauce.

title: Marvben (Marrow Bones)
description: Prepared with marrow, bouillon or water, and bouillon.
steps: Order the marrow bones from the butcher in advance.
Scrape the bones well on the outside and place them in cold water for 10 minutes.
Bind the ends with washed small linen cloths.
Place the bones in a pot and cover with bouillon or boiled water, adding one Maggi Bouillon cube for each 1/4 liter (1 pint).
Bring to a boil, then place the pot over low heat and simmer gently for at least one hour; it must not boil hard.
When serving, remove the linen cloths and place the bones on a hot plate, wrap with a warm napkin, and serve as quickly as possible.
Serve with hot toasted rye bread, kitchen salt, grated horseradish, or chopped parsley.

title: Mi-careme-Suppe (Mid-Lenten Soup)
description: A soup made with carrot, parsnip, and onion.
steps: Prepare the flounder as for fillet.
Chop up a carrot, a parsnip and an onion; prepare a bundle of greens as previously shown.
Place these vegetables on the fire in 1.25 quarts of cold water together with the fish and one teaspoon of salt, and bring the whole to a boil.
Gently remove the filet, place it between two plates to cool, and let the soup cook gently.

Cut half a dozen lettuce leaves into small rounds with an instrument such as a core remover, and plunge them for a minute in boiling, well-salted water, then dry them and place in cold water until needed.
Cut some slices of cold boiled beet in the same manner as the lettuce, and treat the filet in the same way; set all this aside until it is needed.
Rub the remainder of the filet through a strainer with a spoon.
Place 1 quart of milk on the fire to boil; place 2 ounces of butter on the fire beside it, and stir into it the same amount of flour.

Now thin this little by little with the boiling milk and with 1 quart of the water in which the vegetables have been cooked; season the soup with a little white pepper and grated nutmeg, and, if needed, with a little more salt.
Stir in the sieved fish and thicken the soup slowly with a whipped egg yolk.
When the soup is ready for serving, add the fish, lettuce and beets, and serve it immediately, so that the strongly contrasting colors do not lose their appearance.

title: Mirabeller (Mirabelle Plums)
description: Prepared with mirabelle plums, powdered sugar, and cognac.
steps: These small yellow plums must not be completely ripe.
Pour boiling water over them, then cold water.
Boil sugar and water to a thin syrup and add the mirabelles, giving them just one boil.
Remove the plums and place in a jar, and cook down the syrup before pouring it hot over the fruit.
Cover the preserve immediately.
After 2 days, pour off the syrup to cook down further, and add 1/4 dl cognac as soon as the pot is removed from heat, then immediately pour the syrup over the mirabelles and seal.
Mirabelles are excellent for making into compote.

steps: Mix all these spices into some of the vinegar before adding the remaining vinegar.
Cover the jar with a lid or tie it shut with parchment paper and let it stand for 3 to 4 weeks, but it must be stirred regularly in the meantime.
Dry the fresh vegetables in a cloth and they must be completely dry before being placed in the vinegar, gradually as they appear during the course of the summer.
While the pickles are being prepared, stir frequently, and only when all the vegetables have been collected and laid down, distribute them in smaller jars or glasses, which are tied shut and stored.
As they are stored well, the raw vegetables become sufficiently soft.

title: Modne Tomater med Citron (Ripe Tomatoes with Lemon)
description: Prepared with tomatoes, powdered sugar, and lemons.
steps: Tomatoes are available until late autumn but as soon as night frost begins they stop
Ripe but not overripe tomatoes are dried well pricked with a needle and placed in jar in layers with the powdered sugar
The next day the juice is poured off and cooked together with the juice of 2 lemons then poured hot over the tomatoes
The two following days the cooking of the juice is repeated and both times it is poured hot over
To 2 1/2 kg tomatoes dissolve 1/2 teaspoon salicylic acid in a little Cognac and pour this solution over the glasses or jars which are sealed as soon as possible
The salicylic acid must not be omitted with tomatoes as it greatly helps preserve them

title: Mohrenkopf (Moor's Head)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, powdered sugar, and water.
steps: Scald the sweet almonds and chop them somewhat fine and place them in a pan together with the powdered sugar and water. Cook it with constant stirring until the sugar has melted and thereafter become dry and finally the whole has taken on a beautiful light brown color. Then pour another good half pint of water on it and let it cook again until it is like a good, thick porridge. Then pour it into a tin form that must be dipped in cold water, or it will stick to it. Quickly press the sugar firmly in the form with a silver spoon dipped in cold water and let it then stand for 5-6 hours until it is cold, then pour it out of the form.

title: Nedlægning af Sild til Kryddersild (Preparation of Spiced Herring)
description: Prepared with herring, vinegar, and powdered sugar.
steps: Use herring from autumn if possible
Between 1 barrel of herring (which must not be cleaned beforehand), sprinkle 1/2 kg (1 pound) of kitchen salt and let it stand for 12 hours under a light press
Take each herring from the brine, scrape off the scales, lay them again and cover with 1 L (1 pot) of vinegar mixed with 1 L (1 pot) of water
Let stand for another 24 hours
Take up the herrings and let the vinegar drain well before laying them again with the spices

For 1 barrel of herring, combine 1 kg (2 pounds) of Lüneburg salt, 1/4 kg (1/2 pound) of powdered sugar, 15 grams (3 quintals) of Spanish hops, 20 bay leaves, and of ground spices: 25 grams (5 quintals) of cloves, 25 grams (5 quintals) of allspice, 50 grams (10 quintals) of pepper and 15 grams (3 quintals) of saltpeter
Lay the herrings with the back downward in a butter barrel

title: Nedlægning af Sild til Spegesild (Preserved Herring for Curing)
description: Prepared with herring, salt, and butter.

ingredients.name: A wooden barrel or butter churn, well-cleaned and sealed
ingredients.sourceText: A wooden barrel or butter churn, well-cleaned and sealed

steps: Lay fresh, newly caught autumn herring without cleaning them in a barrel and sprinkle with kitchen salt
Leave them for a couple of hours and stir regularly with a stick so that the salt reaches between the herring properly and the blood is drawn out of them
Take them out and drain them, then lay them again in a well-cleaned and sealed butter churn
Lay the herring with the back downward and pack them in tight layers, between which is sprinkled at least {{source-2}}
The top layer must be salt, and over it lay the loose wooden bottom with a good weight on it so that the brine can stand over them
The herring are usable after 4 to 6 weeks

title: Nesselrode Budding (Nesselrode Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cream, egg yolks, and white sugar.

ingredients.name: 1 pail sweet cream, whipped to stiff foam
ingredients.sourceText: 1 pail sweet cream, whipped to stiff foam

steps: Heat 1 pot sweet cream with 8 egg yolks, 1/2 stick vanilla, and {{source-3}}, stirring well while bringing to a boil.
Pour out when done and while still warm, add 3 pails Madeira and 6 quintals dissolved isinglass.

Before it cools completely, stir in 1 pail sweet cream whipped to stiff foam, as well as a handful of finely chopped candied citron, an equal amount of cleaned raisins without pits, and some candied strawberries without juice.
In a mold, layer candied strawberries at the bottom, then a layer of the mixture, then again a layer of jam, and so forth until the mold is full.
Let the pudding stand for several hours in a cold place or freeze in an ice box.
Quickly dip the mold in hot water, turn it out onto a dish, and serve the pudding with raspberry jelly on top.

title: Norsk Budding (Norwegian Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rice flour, white sugar, and cream.
steps: Cream the rice flour, butter, and white sugar together well and gradually add the thin cream.
Pour this mixture and stir in 18 egg yolks, then add the sweet and bitter almonds blended together, the citron, vanilla, currants, and chopped lemon peel.
Finally fold in the beaten egg whites.
Boil for 2.5 hours.
Serve with sweet sauce; serves 14 persons.

title: Norsk Fiskefars (Norwegian Fish Forcemeat)
description: Prepared with fish, white pepper, and butter.
steps: In Norway, pollack is much used for forcemeat
Split and clean the fish, remove the bone
Scrape very carefully (do not chop) and pound in a mortar until it is like a very fine dough, finally pound it with salt to make it even more tough and cohesive
Stir the cold butter until it is white
Add 2 tablespoons pounded flour, ground white pepper and a little milk until it becomes a soft porridge
When well stirred together, work in the scraped fish and stir the forcemeat with quite small amounts of milk at a time until it reaches proper firmness, which is tested by cooking a test ball
This makes an excellent forcemeat
